A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ecosystem respiration in forested lowland streams is regulated at the reach scale by the abundance of woody material in the stream channel, and this abundance is related to the abundance of woxy material in the riparian area.
the abundance of woody materials is a primary control of ecosystem respiration at the stream reach scale.
stream ecosystem respiration is not only influenced by the hydraulic transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide, but also by the abundance of woody material in the stream channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stream channel form and function are not always coupled, and this decoupling may have important implications for how we model and predict ecosystem function at larger scales.
ecosystem respiration is not related to the same physical variables that are known to influence hydraulic transport and biogeochemical transformations.
the physical form of a stream can influence its functioning, and this influence is likely to be most important at baseflow when there are fewer external controls on metabolism (e.g., discharge).
